endpoint: DISCHARGE: epileptiform activity in slice and electrographic seizures in vivo
system: rat and mouse neonatal hippocampal slice; neonatal rat in vivo EEG
effect_note: Reduced epileptiform activity and electrographic seizures; no effect in NKCC1-KO slices or with GABA-A block, so the slice effect is target-controlled. No functional/cognitive endpoint measured in this source.
locator_quote: Bumetanide had no effect in the presence of the GABA(A)-R antagonist bicuculline, nor in brain slices from NKCC1-knockout mice.
transfer_conditions: Depolarising GABA (high NKCC1/KCC2 ratio) in the tissue
transfer_breakers: Chloride gradient in Wwox neuron-deleted neocortex unmeasured; efficacy is state-dependent (see later rows)

endpoint: DISCHARGE: recurrent seizure-like events, phenobarbital-resistant
action_on_target: NKCC1 inhibitor with GABA-A positive modulator
system: intact neonatal rat hippocampus in vitro
effect_note: Phenobarbital alone failed in most preparations; the combination abolished seizures in most. Add-on logic: a GABA-A potentiator is only effective after the chloride gradient is repaired.
locator_quote: Phenobarbital failed to abolish or depress recurrent seizures in 70% of hippocampi.
transfer_conditions: GABA-A potentiator is the candidate class (clobazam H1); shows state dependence of the potentiator effect
transfer_breakers: Ex vivo; no functional outcome; later in vivo models did not replicate (rows below)

endpoint: DISCHARGE: seizure-like event frequency and chloride accumulation across recurrent seizures
system: intact neonatal rat/mouse (Clomeleon) hippocampus in vitro
effect_note: Recurrent seizures raise intracellular chloride and invert GABA-A effect; phenobarbital efficacy falls as seizures recur; bumetanide limits accumulation. Efficacy depends on how many seizures have already occurred, i.e. on state, not on the genotype. Function not measured.
locator_quote: bumetanide inhibited seizure-induced neuronal Cl − accumulation and the consequent facilitation of recurrent seizures
transfer_conditions: Seizure-driven chloride loading in an immature network
transfer_breakers: Ex vivo, one laboratory; does not address whether suppressing the loop helps development

endpoint: DISCHARGE: seizure number and EEG power, phenobarbital add-on
action_on_target: NKCC1 inhibitor with GABA-A positive modulator
system: neonatal rat in vivo, hypoxia-induced seizures
effect_note: Combination cut seizure incidence by roughly three quarters and completely suppressed seizures in about half; phenobarbital alone was partial.
locator_quote: the combination of phenobarbital with low dose bumetanide (n = 35) reduced seizure incidence by approximately 75% compared to vehicles
transfer_conditions: Acute symptomatic neonatal seizures with depolarising GABA
transfer_breakers: Acquired hypoxic injury, not a genetic DEE; later independent models gave null (below)

endpoint: DISCHARGE: seizure number/duration, bumetanide alone
system: neonatal rat in vivo, hypoxia-induced seizures
effect_note: Authors state bumetanide alone had little to no efficacy, in contrast to prior reports; only a higher dose moderately attenuated seizures.
locator_quote: bumetanide alone had little to no efficacy in this model
transfer_conditions: Model-dependent NKCC1 role is the authors own explanation
transfer_breakers: Model-to-model variation shows the effect is not a general property of the target

endpoint: FUNCTION-SAFETY: constitutive apoptosis (TUNEL) in naive pups after seizure-suppressing exposure
effect_note: No increase over background at the lower phenobarbital exposure used; contrasts with the apoptosis seen with higher exposure (Bittigau rows). No learning/memory test.
locator_quote: Neither phenobarbital (n = 11) nor high dose bumetanide (n = 11), administered separately or in combination
transfer_conditions: Shows the harm of GABA-A potentiators is exposure-dependent
transfer_breakers: Single exposure, 48 h histology; cognition not tested

endpoint: DISCHARGE: electrographic seizure burden in HIE neonates
system: human newborns with HIE, open-label dose-finding
effect_note: Few infants met the seizure-reduction criterion; trial stopped early for adverse reactions and limited seizure reduction.
locator_quote: The trial was stopped early because of serious adverse reactions and limited evidence for seizure reduction.
transfer_conditions: Human neonatal seizure add-on test of the NKCC1 concept
transfer_breakers: Acquired HIE; no control arm; aminoglycoside co-exposure

endpoint: FUNCTION-SAFETY: hearing in survivors
effect_note: Hearing impairment on auditory testing in a minority of survivors; confounded by aminoglycosides and HIE; a functional harm independent of discharge.
locator_quote: three of 11 surviving infants had hearing impairment confirmed on auditory testing between 17 and 108 days of age
transfer_conditions: Off-target NKCC1 (cochlea) function is a known liability of the class
transfer_breakers: Confounds; not a neurodevelopmental measure

endpoint: DISCHARGE: seizure burden change after dosing, bumetanide vs control
effect_note: Opposite to the open-label trial: greater post-dose reduction in seizure burden in the treated arm, pilot, post hoc, adjusted for a baseline imbalance (treated arm had higher burden). Not powered for efficacy.
locator_quote: demonstrated an additional reduction in seizure burden attributable to bumetanide over phenobarbital without increased serious adverse effects
transfer_conditions: Randomised control present
transfer_breakers: Post hoc analysis; baseline imbalance; pilot size; acquired seizures

endpoint: FUNCTION-SAFETY: hearing impairment in survivors
effect_note: Small imbalance (treated vs none in controls) in a pilot; authors attribute cases to gentamicin and multiorgan disease; no neurodevelopmental follow-up in the text read.
locator_quote: 2 of 26 treated subjects (8%) and 0 of 13 control subjects had hearing impairment
transfer_conditions: Safety signal in the only randomised comparison
transfer_breakers: Counts too small to show a difference; confounded

endpoint: DISCHARGE: seizure occurrence after asphyxia, bumetanide add-on
effect_note: No potentiation of phenobarbital; stated as consistent with the negative human trial.
locator_quote: The data demonstrate that bumetanide does not increase the efficacy of phenobarbital in a model of birth asphyxia
transfer_conditions: Independent laboratory replication of a negative
transfer_breakers: Exposure may be below NKCC1-inhibitory brain level (brain penetration), per the follow-up paper

endpoint: DISCHARGE: seizure occurrence after asphyxia, benzodiazepine arm
control: vehicle; phenobarbital arm that failed after asphyxia
effect_note: Midazolam suppressed seizures before or after asphyxia where phenobarbital given afterwards did not, so a benzodiazepine still acts on discharge in this immature network. Function not measured.
locator_quote: exerted significant antiseizure effects when administered before or after asphyxia
transfer_conditions: Benzodiazepine-site potentiator acting on discharge in the immature brain (clobazam H1 class)
transfer_breakers: Acquired model; short observation window

endpoint: DISCHARGE: seizure incidence, NKCC1 inhibitor arm of a derivative study
effect_note: Raising bumetanide exposure still did not potentiate phenobarbital.
locator_quote: did not potentiate the effect of a submaximal dose
transfer_conditions: Second null from the same model at higher exposure
transfer_breakers: Same laboratory as the preceding null

endpoint: DISCHARGE: seizure incidence, derivative that does not inhibit NKCC1
effect_note: A bumetanide derivative with no NKCC1 inhibition suppressed seizures with phenobarbital: argues the NKCC1 mechanism is not what carries the discharge effect. Pairs with the next row.
locator_quote: a significant suppression of neonatal seizures was determined for combinations of phenobarbital with DIMAEB or, more effectively, bumepamine, which, however, does not inhibit NKCC1
transfer_conditions: Seizure endpoint and a tissue endpoint in the same animals
transfer_breakers: Abstract only; mechanism of bumepamine unknown; hippocampal histology, not behaviour

endpoint: FUNCTION: hippocampal neurodegeneration after asphyxia and seizures (same animals as preceding row)
effect_note: Combination that stopped seizures also prevented hippocampal neurodegeneration: discharge and tissue outcome moved together (cannot say which caused which).
locator_quote: the bumepamine/phenobarbital combination prevented the neurodegenerative consequences of asphyxia and seizures in the hippocampus
transfer_conditions: Both endpoints after the same intervention in the same model
transfer_breakers: Acquired injury where seizures are driven by the insult; no behaviour; abstract only

endpoint: FUNCTION: neuronal survival (apoptotic neurodegeneration) in naive pups
cell_type_or_stage: postnatal day 0-30, most vulnerable first week
effect_note: Increased apoptotic neurodegeneration at plasma levels the authors call relevant for seizure control. Methods list a flumazenil arm; its result was not read. Seizure endpoint not measured, so benefit on discharge cannot be paired.
locator_quote: phenytoin, phenobarbital, diazepam, clonazepam, vigabatrin, and valproate cause apoptotic neurodegeneration in the developing rat brain
transfer_conditions: Benzodiazepine-site potentiators in a developing cortex; WWOX window is neonatal
transfer_breakers: Naive brain; exposure-dependent (see Cleary null at lower phenobarbital); no behaviour

endpoint: FUNCTION: neuronal survival in naive pups
effect_note: Listed among agents causing apoptosis in the abstract; doses and per-drug histology for vigabatrin not read beyond the methods listing.
locator_quote: phenytoin, phenobarbital, diazepam, clonazepam, vigabatrin, and valproate cause apoptotic neurodegeneration in the developing rat brain
transfer_conditions: GABA-raising mechanism distinct from direct receptor potentiation
transfer_breakers: Abstract-level for this drug

endpoint: FUNCTION: neuronal survival in 7-day-old rats (region-level counts)
action_on_target: Na-channel blocker; GABA-A positive modulator; mixed
effect_note: Table 1: degenerating-cell fraction higher than vehicle in most of 16 regions for all three drugs, e.g. laterodorsal thalamus about 0.3% vehicle versus 2.6, 9.9, 15.9%.
locator_quote: Phenytoin, phenobarbital, and valproate increase the rate of apoptosis in the brain of 7-day-old rats
transfer_conditions: Generic reduction of network activity in the first postnatal week
transfer_breakers: Naive brain; cortex II/IV involvement is the relevant region

endpoint: FUNCTION: neuronal survival, protection arm
effect_note: Estradiol ameliorated drug-induced apoptosis: the harm is separable from the discharge effect and can be modified.
locator_quote: ameliorates AED-induced apoptotic neurodegeneration
transfer_conditions: Indicates harm runs through neurotrophin/survival signalling
transfer_breakers: Not a seizure model

endpoint: FUNCTION: neuronal survival in naive pups, NMDAR agent
effect_note: A few hours of NMDAR blockade triggered widespread apoptosis; the NMDAR class that stops bursts carries the same window-dependent liability.
locator_quote: Blockade of N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) glutamate receptors for only a few hours during late fetal or early neonatal life triggered widespread apoptotic neurodegeneration
transfer_conditions: Applies to the NMDAR thread (GluN2B NAM arms of INV-03/04)
transfer_breakers: Non-selective channel blockers; GluN2B-selective agents not tested here

endpoint: FUNCTION: hippocampal inhibitory synaptic maturation (mIPSC frequency, depolarising network events)
system: rat CA1 slices after neonatal in vivo exposure
effect_note: Treated group lacked the normal rise in mIPSC frequency between P14 and P29 and retained giant depolarising potentials: delayed circuit maturation after a GABA-A potentiator.
locator_quote: the phenobarbital-exposed group did not display a developmental increase in mIPSC frequency
transfer_conditions: Direct circuit-maturation endpoint relevant to the Wwox inhibitory deficit
transfer_breakers: Naive rats; seizure endpoint absent; phenobarbital is not a benzodiazepine

endpoint: FUNCTION: adult associative learning and sensorimotor gating
effect_note: Passive-avoidance learning and prepulse inhibition impaired; reward conditioning not changed.
locator_quote: Likewise, we found deficits in associative learning in adult rats exposed to PB as pups.
transfer_conditions: Cognitive endpoint after a brief early exposure
transfer_breakers: Naive brain; harm size depends on exposure window

endpoint: FUNCTION: adult learning and memory (passive avoidance)
effect_note: Phenobarbital produced the learning deficit; retigabine, tested in the same design, did not (next row).
locator_quote: We found that phenobarbital, but not retigabine, induced deficits in learning/memory in the passive avoidance task.
transfer_conditions: Head-to-head of GABA-A potentiator vs Kv7 opener on one function endpoint
transfer_breakers: Retigabine half-life shorter, so exposure unequal (authors note)

endpoint: FUNCTION: adult learning and memory (passive avoidance)
effect_note: No learning deficit in the passive-avoidance task; seizure endpoint not tested in the same animals.
locator_quote: We found that phenobarbital, but not retigabine, induced deficits in learning/memory in the passive avoidance task.
transfer_conditions: Kv7 opener arm of IT13 P3a
transfer_breakers: Shorter exposure; one learning task

endpoint: FUNCTION: anxiety-like behaviour in adulthood
effect_note: Increased anxiety-like behaviour in two of three tasks: the Kv7 opener is not neutral for non-seizure function, though subtler than phenobarbital.
locator_quote: Our finding that retigabine increased anxiety-like behavior in two of the three tasks (open field and light-dark, but not the elevated plus maze)
transfer_conditions: Non-seizure liability of the Kv7 opener class
transfer_breakers: Behavioural, not circuit; naive pups

endpoint: FUNCTION: social interaction and context-dependent fear memory
control: wild-type mice, vehicle, one-week washout reversal
effect_note: Rescued deficits fully while on drug and the effect reversed after washout; wild-type unaffected. Authors infer that the deficits come from reduced GABAergic transmission, not from recurrent seizures. A repair-type result for a measured inhibitory loss, but acute and adult.
locator_quote: a single low-dose clonazepam injection completely rescued deficits in social interactions and fear-associated contextual memory without sedative or anxiolytic effects
transfer_conditions: Inhibitory loss as the lesion; benzodiazepine site potentiation; function endpoint
transfer_breakers: Adult acute dosing; no seizure endpoint with it; Scn1a lesion is in interneurons, Wwox lesion locus unmeasured

endpoint: DISCHARGE: not measured with the same drug in the same experiment
effect_note: The paper separates function from seizures by argument, not by measurement: the same low exposure was chosen to avoid sedation. Marks a missing paired endpoint; not a null.
locator_quote: these comorbidities in DS mice are not caused by recurrent seizure-induced excitotoxicity
transfer_conditions: Records that function and discharge need separate measurement
transfer_breakers: Authors inference, not a data row

endpoint: FUNCTION: social interaction dose-response
system: BTBR mouse (idiopathic autism model, not an epilepsy model)
effect_note: Bell-shaped: benefit at the low end lost at higher exposure; the alpha1-preferring potentiator had the opposite effect. Functional benefit of a benzodiazepine-site agent is graded and subtype-dependent.
locator_quote: Interestingly, the improved social interactions in BTBR mice was lost at higher doses of clonazepam
transfer_conditions: Graded potentiation; matches the IT14 note that restoration is not guaranteed
transfer_breakers: Not an epilepsy model; no seizure endpoint

endpoint: DISCHARGE: infantile spasm frequency (behavioural and electroclinical)
stress_or_context: lesion plus chemical hit, cortical mTOR activation
effect_note: Dose-related reduction in spasms; only the dose that normalised perilesional pS6 worked.
locator_quote: There was a dose-related reduction in the frequency of behavioral and electroclinical spasms.
transfer_conditions: mTOR as measured driver in the model (pS6 raised)
transfer_breakers: WWOX mTOR status in neurons not shown here; this lesion is acquired plus pathway

endpoint: FUNCTION: learning and memory (Barnes maze) in model pups
effect_note: Early cessation of spasms partially improved the learning deficit, measured more than 10 days after the last dose; same animals as the discharge row. Benefit on discharge and on function in one model.
locator_quote: Early cessation of spasms by rapamycin partially improved learning and memory deficits of DLP pups in the Barnes maze
transfer_conditions: Both endpoints, same model, same intervention
transfer_breakers: Partial; benefit tied to cause-directed (mTOR) action, not to discharge suppression alone

endpoint: FUNCTION: learning and memory in control pups (no disease)
effect_note: Same exposure that helped the model pups worsened controls; authors read this as homeostatic control of TORC1 being paramount. A compensatory-range effect: benefit exists only where the pathway is pathologically high.
locator_quote: rapamycin-treated controls had worse performance in the Barnes maze than vehicle-treated controls
transfer_conditions: Tests whether an agent harms a non-diseased circuit
transfer_breakers: Healthy control; WWOX deficit state of mTOR unknown

endpoint: DISCHARGE: other seizure types and interictal abnormalities
effect_note: Cognitive benefit appeared without any change in other seizure types or interictal spikes: function improved while most of the discharge did not, so discharge count is a poor proxy for function here.
locator_quote: There was no significant effect of rapamycin on other types of electroclinical seizures or on the interictal epileptic abnormalities
transfer_conditions: Dissociates symptomatic response from function
transfer_breakers: Single model, single lab

endpoint: FUNCTION: cortical interneuron survival (PV and SST density at P21)
intervention: chemogenetic inhibition of pyramidal cells during the interneuron death window
action_on_target: hM4Di-based silencing (genetic receptor plus inert ligand)
control: control animals with the same ligand
effect_note: Dampening pyramidal activity in the critical window reduced PV and SST interneuron density; activity-dependent survival, so network silencing early costs inhibitory cells. This is a mechanism by which suppression of activity could worsen a deficit; it was not tested in an epilepsy model.
locator_quote: dampening the activity of pyramidal cells decreases the density of PV+ and SST+ interneurons at P21 compared to controls
transfer_conditions: Wwox neuron-deleted cortex has low Pvalb transcript and early postnatal window overlap
transfer_breakers: Chemogenetic silencing is not a drug; no epilepsy context

endpoint: FUNCTION: cortical interneuron survival (PV and SST density at P21)
intervention: chemogenetic activation of pyramidal cells during the interneuron death window
control: control animals with the same ligand
effect_note: Raising pyramidal activity in the same window prevented interneuron death and raised PV and SST density: moderate excitatory drive is a survival signal for inhibitory neurons.
locator_quote: increasing the activity of pyramidal cells during the period of interneuron cell death prevents this process
transfer_conditions: Opposite-direction control of the preceding row
transfer_breakers: Excess drive in an epilepsy would add excitotoxic cost, not tested

endpoint: COMPENSATION: excitatory synaptic drive onto pyramidal cells after interneuron Kv7 loss
control: pyramidal-cell Kcnq2 knockout (no change in mEPSC)
effect_note: Raised excitatory drive appears as a homeostatic response to increased GABAergic signalling, so some hyperexcitability is built by the network after a change in inhibition rather than being the primary lesion.
locator_quote: perhaps as homeostatic compensation for the increased GABAergic signaling we observe
transfer_conditions: Network-level plasticity after an inhibitory change
transfer_breakers: Genetic loss in adult interneurons; authors word it as possible

endpoint: DISCHARGE: latency to chemoconvulsant seizure
intervention: deletion of Kcnq2 in PV interneurons
effect_note: Seizure latency shortened (more excitable) with the same genotype that shows the homeostatic synaptic change; a knockout, not an inhibitor.
locator_quote: with a significantly reduced latency to seizure onset when compared to Pvalb;Kcnq2+/+ mice
transfer_conditions: Kv7 loss in inhibitory cells as a hyperexcitability route
transfer_breakers: A knockout does not predict a Kv7 opener effect

endpoint: DISCHARGE: evoked and spontaneous seizures, opener arm
effect_note: Opener strongly reduced evoked-seizure susceptibility; function/cognition not reported in the abstract.
locator_quote: Kcnq2RW/+ mice displayed increased susceptibility to evoked seizures, which was dramatically ameliorated by treatment with the novel KCNQ opener pynegabine (HN37)
transfer_conditions: Opener efficacy in a Kv7 loss model; Kcnq2 lesion is on the target
transfer_breakers: Target is the mutated channel; WWOX lesion is not Kv7

endpoint: FUNCTION: motor, anxiety and cognitive tests after chronic exposure
action_on_target: T-type Ca2+ channel blocker (ethosuximide); alpha2delta ligand (gabapentin)
effect_note: No adverse effect and no benefit on tested behaviours; the study was designed around KCNJ6, not seizures. No developmental seizure model with a paired cognitive endpoint was found for the T-type class.
locator_quote: Neither drug significantly affected sensorimotor abilities, motor coordination or spontaneous activity in TS and CO mice.
transfer_conditions: Only evidence found on a cognitive safety of the T-type blocker in developing mice
transfer_breakers: Not a seizure model; mice not exposed neonatally

endpoint: DISCHARGE: spasm cessation (initial vs final)
effect_note: Initial spasm control was better with hormone treatment, not different by 12-14 months. Comparison of two active treatments.
locator_quote: Hormone treatment controls spasms better than does vigabatrin initially, but not at 12-14 months of age.
transfer_conditions: Developmental epilepsy, seizure and development both measured
transfer_breakers: Human; no untreated arm; etiology mix

endpoint: FUNCTION: developmental outcome (adaptive behaviour score, 14 months)
effect_note: Overall score did not differ even though initial spasm control did; benefit on discharge did not carry into function overall.
locator_quote: Mean VABS score did not differ significantly
transfer_conditions: Pairs with the discharge row of the same trial
transfer_breakers: No untreated arm

endpoint: FUNCTION: developmental outcome at about 4 years
effect_note: Overall no significant difference; the better development in those without an identified aetiology (allocated hormone) persisted (borderline, subgroup), implying that the cause governs whether discharge control tracks development.
locator_quote: For all 77 infants, development and epilepsy outcomes were not significantly different between the two treatment groups.
transfer_conditions: Longer follow-up of development versus seizure control
transfer_breakers: Telephone questionnaire; subgroup, small n; loss to follow-up

system: two WWOX-null children with West syndrome (repository record CLAIM 031)
effect_note: Repository record, not re-read at source: development remained profoundly impaired despite improved epileptic activity, with the qualifier in some of these cases; n=2, uncontrolled; ordering of onset not shown for both children. Counted once.

transfer_conditions: Same genotype class; direct
